title: Triangulation, Volume, and Symmetries of the Dihedral Group Analogue of the Permutohedron
summary: We study the analogue of the permutohedron for the dihedral group, which we call the dihedral permutohedron. We determine the facet structure of the dihedral permutohedron, use the facet structure to construct a triangulation, and determine a nice combinatorial formula for the volume of the dihedral permutohedron. Lastly, we find a family of interesting unimodular affine symmetries of the odd dihedral permutohedron.

title: Two q-Deformations of Narayana Polynomials: Rogers Moments, Hankel Positivity, and q-Narayana Kernels
summary: We study two $q$-deformations of the continuous interpolation between type $B$ and shifted type $A$ Narayana polynomials, both constructed from the continuous $q$-ultraspherical (Rogers) functional. The first consists of affine moments of ordinary powers. For fixed $0<q<1$ and $-1<β<1$, we prove coefficientwise Hankel total positivity in the polynomial variable by a continuant comparison criterion. We also determine leading continuants, Hankel determinants, and extreme coefficients of arbitrary Hankel minors. The second deformation uses Askey--Wilson basis products and yields a basic-hypergeometric Narayana kernel. We give two independent moment evaluations and prove that its row polynomials have simple negative zeros and are $γ$-positive after palindromic normalization. An Askey--Wilson integral with base $q^2$ gives a continuous-parameter extension and a moment proof of the Krattenthaler--Wachs super $q$-Narayana expansion, including its integrality. An ordinary-power expansion also proves Pan's Touchard identity. For fixed $0<q<1$ and $θ>-1$, we prove total positivity of the kernel triangle by a Jackson $q$-Bessel--Edrei factorization and strict total positivity of its associated square by a discrete moment representation. This gives a simultaneous $(θ,q)$-extension of Wang--Yang's theorems for type $A$ and type $B$ Narayana triangles and squares. We further establish coefficientwise total nonnegativity in $q$ through order two for the endpoint triangles. An exact triangular change of basis links the two deformations and explains their common classical limit.

title: Low-degree filtrations in ordinary and Lagrangian Grassmannian cohomology
summary: We prove the Hilbert-series formulas conjectured by Reiner--Tudose and by the Polymath Jr. Grassmannian group for the subalgebras of ordinary and Lagrangian Grassmannian cohomology generated in bounded degree. We determine the finite coefficient images underlying the proofs, together with the kernels of the coefficient and cancellation maps. We also construct bases adapted to the auxiliary ideal filtrations and identify the cancellation layers, as modules, with shifts of finite complete-intersection algebras. First-order deformations give the derivative inclusions needed to recover the filtration increments. We disprove the two ordinary basis conjectures of the Polymath group. For every $r\ge 2$, the span of each prescribed family has codimension one in weight $3r+2$ of $H^{2*}(\operatorname{Gr}(2,3r+1);\mathbb Q)$; replacing one index gives a basis in each of these components. More generally, each prescribed two-row family has codimension at most one in every weight. Weights are half the cohomological degrees, and all coefficients are rational.

title: From Wheel to Jahangir graphs: spectra and energy under structured edge deletion
summary: The energy of a graph, introduced by Gutman, is defined as the sum of the absolute values of the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix. In this work we study how the energy of the Wheel graph $W_n$ changes when a specific set of spokes is removed. The resulting graphs are precisely the Jahangir graphs $J_{m,n}$, where m divides n, and which may also be viewed as the Cycle graph $C_n$ together with an additional vertex adjacent to certain vertices of $C_n$ in a cyclic pattern. We determine the spectra of $J_{2,n}$, $J_{4,n}$, and $J_{6,n}$ by exploiting a factorization of their characteristic polynomials arising from equitable partitions. This yields explicit closed formulas for their energies. Moreover, under certain conditions, we establish the following monotonicity chain: \[\mathcal{E}(C_n) \;\leq\; \mathcal{E}(J_{6,n}) \;\leq\; \mathcal{E}(J_{4,n}) \;\leq\; \mathcal{E}(J_{2,n}) \;\leq\; \mathcal{E}(W_n).\]

title: Tree-independence number VIII. 3PC-free graphs have logarithmic tree-independence number
summary: A three-path-configuration is a graph consisting of three pairwise internally vertex-disjoint paths, the union of every two of which is an induced cycle of length at least four. A graph is 3PC-free if no induced subgraph of it is a three-path-configuration. We show that 3PC-free graphs have logarithmic tree-independence number, which is asymptotically best possible.

title: A sporadic simplicial arrangement of $51$ lines
summary: We construct a sporadic simplicial arrangement of $51$ lines in the real projective plane. It is obtained from the icosahedral arrangement $\mathcal{A}(21,2)$ by adjoining the $30$ images of the line $y+\sqrt{\varphi}\,z=0$ under the rotation group of the icosahedron, where $\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$. Its intersection multiplicities are $t_2=120$, $t_3=190$, $t_5=36$, and $t_6=15$, with all other $t_r$ zero. These counts give equality in Melchior's inequality and hence prove simpliciality. The arrangement is irreducible, belongs to neither of the two known infinite families of irreducible simplicial arrangements, and is not supersolvable. It therefore disproves the $37$-line bound for sporadic arrangements conjectured by Cuntz and Mücksch. We give explicit coordinates, a finite incidence certificate, a geometric explanation of the parameter $\sqrt{\varphi}$, and a standalone exact-arithmetic verifier.

title: The domination number of the $k$-token graph of the complete bipartite graph $K_{m,n}$
summary: This paper is about token graphs and domination number. Let $G=(X,E)$ denote an undirected graph that is connected, with no loops or multiple edges, vertex set $X$, and edge set $E$. Pick a positive integer $k\leq \vert X\vert$. The $k$-token graph of $G$, denoted by $F_k(G)$, is defined as follows. The vertex set $\mathcal{X}$ consists of all $k$-subsets of $X$. Two vertices $x,y\in \mathcal{X}$ are adjacent whenever the symmetric difference of $x$ and $y$ consists of two vertices that form an edge in $E$. In this paper, we compute the exact value for the domination number of $F_2(K_{m,n})$ where $K_{m,n}$ is the complete bipartite graph with parameters $m,n$. We present some bounds for the domination number of $F_k(K_{m,n})$ when $k\geq 3$.

title: On the Number of Iterations in a Kruskal-Type Process
summary: Motivated by the Kruskal counting procedure, this paper investigates a combinatorial elimination process defined on a deck consisting of $m$ copies of each value $1,2,\ldots,n$. Starting from an arbitrary arrangement of the $mn$ cards, the process repeatedly removes a number of consecutive cards equal to the value of the first remaining card. This generates a sequence of elimination steps whose length determines $T$, representing the total number of iterations required to exhaust the deck. The main objective of this paper is to analyze an upper bound $σ(m,n)$ for $T$, valid for every initial configuration of the deck, and to show that this bound is attained by a specific configuration.

title: Every tournament of dichromatic number $10 k^2$ has a vertex whose out-neighborhood has dichromatic number more than $k$
summary: The dichromatic number of a tournament is the minimum number of colors needed to color the vertices so that no directed cycle is monochromatic. Nguyen, Scott, and Seymour (2025) asked whether every tournament with dichromatic number $2k$ has a vertex whose out-neighborhood induces a subtournament of dichromatic number at least $k$. We answer their question negatively by finding an example with dichromatic number $Ω(k^2)$. Furthermore, this quadratic bound is tight up to a constant factor; we show that for every integer $k \geq 1$, every tournament of dichromatic number $Ω(k^2)$ contains a vertex whose out-neighborhood induces a subtournament of dichromatic number more than $k$. This improves the previous best bound $\mathcal{O}(k^2\log k)$ due to Colinot and Newman (2026). To show this, we prove that every tournament of fractional dichromatic number $c$ has a dominating set of size at most $5c-1$. The proof uses Brouwer's fixed point theorem.

title: Non-trivial intersecting families for direct products
summary: A family of sets is intersecting if any two of its sets intersect, and non-trivial intersecting if there is not any element which appears in every set of the family. The study of intersection problems (or Erdős-Ko-Rado problems) on families of sets is one of the most important topics in extremal combinatorics. A natural extension of the Erdős-Ko-Rado problem in direct products setting was introduced by Frankl, and developed by Alon and Katona et al. In 2018, Kwan, Sudakov and Vieira [J. Combin. Theory, Ser. A 156 (2018), 44--60] determine the maximum size of a non-trivial intersecting direct product family under the assumption that the sizes of all parts are sufficiently large relative to the set sizes in all parts. Meanwhile, they raised the question of whether this result holds for the size of each part which depends only on its corresponding set size, and the question of characterizing the extremal families. In the present paper, we answere these two questions. Furthermore, the bounds on the size of each part in our result are best possible.1
comment: 19 pages. No Generative AI tools were used at any stage

title: Proofs of Li, Wang and Guo's conjectures on (signless) Laplacian spectral radius
summary: Let $μ(G)$ and $q(G)$ be the Laplacian and signless Laplacian spectral radii of a graph $G$. Li, Wang and Guo (2026) conjectured that, if $H$ with $|V(H)|\geq 1$ is an induced subgraph of a graph $G$, then $μ(G)\le\max\limits_{v\in V(H)}μ(H_v^t)$ and $q(G)\le\max\limits_{v\in V(H)}q(H_v^t)$, where $t=e(G)-e(H)$ and $H_v^t$ is the graph obtained from $H$ by adding $t$ pendant edges to $v\in V(H)$. We prove this conjecture by establishing a spectral comparison theorem for a broader family of positive semidefinite graph matrices which includes the Laplacian and signless Laplacian matrices. We also characterize all equality cases for the prescribed subgraph $H$ with $e(H)\geq 1$ and $t\geq 1$.

title: General Criterion for a Poset to Admit a Partition Into $ω$-Chains
summary: Given a poset $P$ with no maximal element the question naturally arises of when $P$ can be partitioned into $ω$-chains. In this paper we give general criterion for when this can be done. We show that in the case when a poset with no maximal element is countable or a well-founded forest, then it can always be partitioned into $ω$-chains. We then introduce the lifting property for posets with no maximal element and show that a poset can be partitioned into $ω$-chains if and only if it has the lifting property.

title: Pappus configurations in the Hall plane
summary: In this paper, we investigate Pappus configurations in the finite affine Hall plane. In particular, we show that for any two lines $\ell_1,\ell_2$ and for any triple of points on $\ell_1$ there is a triple of points on $\ell_2$ that are contained in a Pappus configuration, thus improving on the results of [F. Lazebnik and L. Leshock. On Pappus configurations in Hall planes. Des. Codes Cryptogr. 90 (2022), 1203--1219.].

title: On a conjecture concerning two-stack sortable permutations
summary: The two-stack sortable permutations of length $n$ are known to be equinumerous with permutations of length $n$ avoiding the dashed patterns $3\text{-}1\text{-}4\text{-}2$ and $2\text{-}41\text{-}3$. In this paper, we confirm an intriguing conjecture posed by Claesson, Kitaev, and Steingrímsson, which asserts that the quadruple $(\comp,\asc,\ldr,\rmax)$ is equidistributed on these two permutation classes. Here $\comp$ and $\asc$ count the number of components and ascents, respectively, $\ldr$ denotes the length of the initial decreasing run, and $\rmax$ denotes the number of right-to-left maxima. This is accomplished by constructing bijections between two-stack sortable permutations and $β(1,0)$-trees.

title: Integer Flows on Cyclic Covers of Graphs
summary: Graph covers preserve the local structure of a graph while allowing its global structure to change substantially. In this paper, we study how such changes in cyclic covers affect nowhere-zero flow properties. For a fixed integer $\ell \ge 2$, we show that for every bridgeless graph $G$, there exists an $\ell$-fold cyclic cover of $G$ that admits a nowhere-zero $3$-flow if $\ell$ is even and a nowhere-zero $4$-flow if $\ell$ is odd. These bounds are best possible in general. For odd $\ell$, we further investigate which bridgeless graphs admit an $\ell$-fold cyclic cover with a nowhere-zero $3$-flow.

title: Small covers and the Four Color Theorem
summary: We give a combinatorial proof that every simple convex $3$-polytope admits a small cover without using the Four Color Theorem. We also prove that the assertion that every simple plane triangulation admits a mod~$2$ characteristic function with at most five values is equivalent to the Four Color Theorem.

title: The Local Dyadic Conjecture
summary: A rational with denominator a power of two is said to be dyadic. A long standing conjecture of Paul Seymour predicts that for an ideal clutter, the dual of the set covering problem always admits an optimal solution where all variables take dyadic values. We present a local version of this conjecture, and motivate it by proving an important special case.

title: A proof of Ward's conjecture on Griesmer codes
summary: Let $C$ be an $[n,k,d]_q$ Griesmer code, where $q=p^f$ with $p$ prime, and write $e=ν_p(d)$. Ward conjectured that $C$ is $p^{\max\{0,e-f+1\}}$-divisible. In this paper, we prove this conjecture.

title: Counting and constructing Latin tableaux
summary: Latin tableaux generalize Latin squares to Young diagrams and have interesting connections to linear algebra and Rota's basis conjecture. Conjecturally, a partition admits Latin tableaux if and only if it belongs to a special class called wide partitions. We prove that various classes of wide partitions admit Latin tableaux. We extend these classes further by showing that the number of Latin tableaux is weakly increasing over certain operations on wide partitions. Additionally, we establish an explicit formula for the number of Latin tableaux using (0,1)-matrices and matrix permanents.

title: An entropy proof of the commonality of apices of trees
summary: A graph $H$ is called common if the number of monochromatic copies of $H$ in a $2$-edge-colouring of a large complete graph is asymptotically minimized by the random colouring with an equal proportion of each colour. Grzesik, Lee, Lidický and Volec conjectured that every $k$-apex of any connected Sidorenko graph is common. Recently, Kr{á}l', Krnc and Lamaison proved that the $k$-apex of any tree is common for $k\leq 5$. In this paper, we extend their result by showing that for every positive integer $k$, the $k$-apex of any tree or any forest with average degree at least one is common. Our proof involves an application of the entropy method.

title: Avoiding two cycles in Avoider--Enforcer games
summary: We study the strict and monotone $(1:b)$ Avoider--Enforcer games on the edges of the complete graph $K_n$. We prove that, for integers $n\ge2$ and $b\ge6n$, Avoider can keep his graph a forest after every move, except possibly the last. Thus, his final graph contains at most one cycle. This answers Question~10 of Clemens, Ehrenmüller, Person, and Tran, which asks whether a bias linear in $n$ is sufficient.

title: A Computer-Assisted Proof that R(5,10;5,8)=21 for the Generalized Threshold Ramsey Number
summary: We prove that the generalized threshold Ramsey number R(5,10;5,8) equals 21. This number corresponds to the set Ramsey number r_5(10,8) introduced by Harborth. The proof is computer-assisted. We first enumerate all (4,6;5,8)-good and (5,10;4,4)-good graphs. Then we apply the lucky-vertex inequality derived from the McKay--Radziszowski edge identity to filter candidate pairs for a gluing search, and encode the remaining cases as SAT instances. The search yields exactly 17 non-isomorphic (5,10;5,8;20)-good graphs. Finally, we exclude all one-vertex extensions of these 17 graphs, which proves that no (5,10;5,8;21)-good graph exists.Additionally, we update the tabulation of small set Ramsey numbers r_5(m,n) for 1 <= m,n <= 10.

title: Connected Coloring Games on Corona Products of Graphs
summary: We study the connected coloring game on corona products of graphs. For connected graphs $G$ and $H$, we prove the sharp upper bound $χ_{cg}(G\circ H)\leq\max\{Δ(G),Δ(H)+1\}+1$ and establish a further bound using the Bob-start ordinary coloring game on the second factor. We show that the difference between the Alice-start and Bob-start connected game chromatic numbers can be arbitrarily large in either direction. We further prove that a connected subgraph may have arbitrarily larger connected game chromatic number than its ambient connected graph, and that $χ_{cg}(G\circ H)$ cannot be bounded in terms of $χ_{cg}(G)$ and $χ_{cg}(H)$ alone, even when both factors have connected game chromatic number $2$. We also obtain corona products for which the difference $χ_g-χ_{cg}$ is arbitrarily large and construct infinitely many connected graphs with $χ_g<χ_{cg}$. Finally, for corona products of trees, we prove the universal upper bound $5$, characterize those attaining the value $3$, give structural sufficient conditions for the value $4$, and exhibit a broad family attaining the value $5$.

title: Small and Large Quasi-Kernels in General Digraphs
summary: In a digraph $D$, a set $Q$ of vertices is a quasi-kernel if $Q$ is an independent set and every vertex in $D$ can be reached from $Q$ via at most two edges. The small quasi-kernel conjecture by Erdős and Székely predicts that every source-free $n$-vertex digraph contains a quasi-kernel of size at most $n - n/2$. Chvátal and Lovász' 1974 work implies a bound of $n - \sqrt{n}+1$. In 2024, Sprio shows the bound $n - \frac{1}{4} \sqrt{n \log_2 n}$. We show that there always is a quasi-kernel of size at most $n - \frac{1}{51}n^{2/3} / \ln^{2/3}(n)$. For the related large quasi-kernel conjecture by Spiro, we show that there always is a quasi-kernel $Q$ with $|N^+[Q]| \ge 0.2917 \cdot n^{2/3} / \ln^{2/3}(n)$.
comment: Preprint submitted to the Journal of Graph Theory

title: Spanning bipartite quadrangulations in even triangulations of real projective spaces
summary: We study spanning quadrangulations of even triangulations of real projective spaces, using the higher-dimensional notion of quadrangulation introduced by Kaiser and Stehlík. We prove that every even triangulation of $\RP^d$, where $d\ge 2$, admits a spanning bipartite quadrangulation. Moreover, such a triangulation admits a spanning non-bipartite quadrangulation if and only if it is not balanced; if it is balanced, every spanning quadrangulation is bipartite. Our proofs use coloring monodromy: its orbits yield bipartite quadrangulations, while a covering-space construction gives non-bipartite ones. %In dimension three, a bipartite quadrangulation can always be chosen to induce $K_{2,2}$ on each tetrahedron. More generally, we establish a sufficient condition for the existence of spanning bipartite quadrangulations on closed manifolds in terms of the monodromy action, and derive a consequence involving the fundamental group.

title: Modulating flow polynomials and parity bias in homological walk counting
summary: Long weighted walks seem to sample mod-$t$ flows uniformly, but at even moduli a persistent parity bias survives. Writing $C_G(t)$ for the flow polynomial of a connected graph $G$ of genus $g$, the proportion of nowhere-zero flows under uniform sampling is $C_G(t)/t^g$. For arbitrary positive directed weights and all moduli, we determine the exact leading corrections for both closed walks and nonbacktracking closed walks, which we call circuits. Only the circuit result requires $g\ge2$. For closed walks, the canonical character governs the leading correction through the canonical modulating flow polynomial $D_G$; for circuits, the period character, when it exists, governs the leading correction through the period modulating flow polynomial $D_{G,η}$. At even moduli these give parity-dependent corrections: the two mechanisms coincide on nonbipartite graphs and separate only in the bipartite circuit problem. More generally, each integral-homology character $ζ$ determines a balanced-dichromatic specialization $D_{G,ζ}$. These polynomials form a character-indexed family whose finite-order members give Fourier coefficients of the nowhere-zero flow set and whose retained edge sets are the central sets of a gain semimatroid. We further show that $D_G$ is a cycle-matroid invariant and a signed-Tutte specialization satisfying signed deletion-contraction. Finally, an integral nowhere-zero approximation theorem implies that asymptotically almost every weighted circuit traverses every edge.
comment: 38 pages, 2 figures. Computational notebook and PDF export included as ancillary files

title: Topological degree of fewnomial maps
summary: We study the topological degree on the positive orthant of a map $F:\mathbb{R}^n_{>0}\to\mathbb{R}^n$ whose components are real polynomials, possibly with real exponents, with the same support $\mathcal{A}$ of $N=n+k+1$ monomials. This degree is well defined under a half-space condition on the columns of the coefficient matrix indexed by the faces of the Newton polytope, which holds for generic exponents and coefficients. We give three formulas for it, all in terms of signs of maximal minors. The first one is a Viro formula: the degree is a signed count of the simplices of a regular triangulation of $\mathcal{A}$ which are positively decorated in the sense of Bihan, Santos and Spaenlehauer. The second one is a sum over the facets of the Newton polytope, and the third one a sum over the vertices of the polyhedron of the Gale dual system. As a consequence, the degree only depends on the oriented matroids of the exponent and coefficient matrices restricted to the vertices of the Newton polytope. We also obtain a Descartes rule of signs for the degree and, in the generic case, the upper bound $|°F|<\frac12\min(M(n,N),M(k,N))$, where $M(d,N)$ is the largest number of facets of a $d$-polytope with $N$ vertices. This bound is sharp when $n=2$ or $k=2$. Using the H-duality of Bihan, Dickenstein and Forsgård, we show that the set of possible degrees is symmetric in $n$ and $k$. Since a nonzero degree forces a positive zero, our formulas give sign conditions for the existence of positive solutions, as well as parity statements for their number.

title: The three-colour bipartite Ramsey number of sufficiently long even cycles
summary: For a bipartite graph $H$, let $\operatorname{br}_3(H)$ be the least integer $N$ such that every three-colouring of $K_{N,N}$ contains a monochromatic copy of $H$. We prove that $\operatorname{br}_3(C_{2n})=3n$ for all sufficiently large $n$, and give the lower bound for every $n\ge2$. For the upper bound, we reduce a counterexample to a finite rational weighted profile. Cycle extension and vertex-cover arguments force the critical components to have six unique minimum covers which partition the profile. The remaining component supports give a contradiction.

title: Permutations, Pattern Covers, Posets and Positivity: Part I: Patterns and Posets
summary: We study permutations covered by overlapping occurrences of a consecutive pattern. Special cases of this have been studied for consecutive patterns and via the cluster method. We study enumeration sequences obtained by repeating a fixed overlap. We elicit many structural properties of such pattern covers, mainly in terms of posets whose linear extensions are in bijection with the permutations in question. The enumeration of these permutations for different patterns gives rise to a great variety of sequences, many classical, but most of them not found in the OEIS. We conjecture that, essentially, all these sequences are moments of probability measures on the real line. We develop an enumerative and order-theoretic framework for this. For overlap 1 we give a generating function whose coefficients enumerate permutations covered by any fixed pattern with any fixed number of occurrences. For overlap at most half the pattern length we derive a polynomial-time enumeration formula. We associate to each pattern, overlap, and number of occurrences a poset whose linear extensions are the corresponding permutations. The regularity of this poset construction makes possible a structural analysis that in many cases leads to enumerative formulas for large classes of patterns. We prove uniform restrictions on the local structure of the Hasse diagrams, describe their branches (pendant chains) in terms of the corresponding patterns, and characterize when the poset is a tree or chain or subdivisions of a grid. Some of these constructions yield explicit families of formulas and explain unexpected equinumerations. In a forthcoming paper we investigate the sequences arising here from a probabilistic perspective, viewing them both as point processes and as moment sequences. We also obtain integral and matrix representations for important overlap 1 and 2 classes of pattern-covering sequences.

title: Nashtopes and their A-discriminants
summary: An $n$-player game in normal form is said to be of format $\boldsymbol{d} = (d_1, \dots, d_n)$ if the $i$-th player has $d_i$ options for $1 \le i \le n$, and is said to be balanced if $d_n - 1 \le \sum_{i=1}^{n-1}(d_i - 1)$. The Nash equilibria of the game correspond to solutions of the system of indifference equations for the game, with payoff differences as coefficients and strategy probabilities as variables. As such, the mixed discriminant of this system gives some information about which games could have an unusual number of totally mixed Nash equilibria. This mixed discriminant can be regarded as an $\mathcal{A}$-discriminant for some matrix $\mathcal{A}$ in the sense of [Gelfand--Kapranov--Zelevinsky 1994], and the convex hull of the columns of $\mathcal{A}$ is a polytope, which we call the Nashtope. We study this $\mathcal{A}$-discriminant for each balanced game format with at least three players. This discriminant is a subset of the Nash discriminant variety introduced in [Abo--Portakal--Sodomaco 2026]. We compute the codimension and degree of this discriminant for all balanced game formats, including on-boundary formats, using the Euler obstruction formula in [Matsui--Takeuchi 2011]. Our $\mathcal{A}$-discriminant locus corresponds to a special multigraded Hurwitz locus studied in [Pratt--Sodomaco--Sturmfels 2026]. As a consequence of [Pokidkin 2026], we obtain the codimensions and degrees of the irreducible components of the Nash discriminant variety for each balanced game format with at least three players, fully resolving Problem 3.8 of [Abo--Portakal--Sodomaco 2026].
comment: 36 pages, 4 tables. Supplementary software documentation is available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23190651

title: A weighted inequality for matroid flats and log-concavity of Whitney numbers
summary: Using the Hodge-Riemann relations for matroid Chow rings, we establish a weighted inequality for flats of a loopless matroid. As applications, we prove the points-lines-planes conjecture and Brylawski's conjecture on the ultra-log-concavity of Whitney numbers of the first kind. We also characterize the cases of equality in both inequalities.

title: Hitting time for loose Hamilton cycles in the random hypergraph process
summary: The random hypergraph process starts with an empty hypergraph on $n$ vertices and adds a uniformly chosen missing edge at each step. For even $n$, we prove that, with high probability, a $3$-uniform loose Hamilton cycle appears when the last isolated vertex disappears. The approach developed here adapts arguments from Kahn's work on perfect matchings. It can also be extended to obtain the corresponding hitting-time theorems for $r=2$ and every fixed $r\ge4$ satisfying $(r-1)\mid n$. Furthermore, it can be used to estimate the numbers of loose Hamilton cycles at these hitting times for every fixed $r\ge2$, up to a factor of $\exp\{o(n)\}$.

title: Compression Formula for Nonattacking Fillings of Non-symmetric Macdonald Polynomials
summary: Macdonald polynomials are an important family of orthogonal polynomials that have applications to statistical physics. Corteel, Mandelshtam, and Williams proved a combinatorial model involving multiline queues for partitions; however, their work does not apply to weak compositions in general. We conjecture a first step towards this direction via a variant of the nonattacking filling model for nonsymmetric Macdonald Polynomials $E_μ$. This new model compresses the classical nonattacking filling model of Haglund, Haiman, and Loehr and mirrors the concept of trivial pairs in the multiline queue model. We prove it for a large family of weak compositions and explain the difficulty of extending this proof to the general case.

title: On $k$-connected Sets in Matroids
summary: In 1966, Tutte defined $k$-connected matroids for each $k \ge 2$. Robertson and Seymour built on Tutte's idea to define tangles as a way to identify highly connected parts of a matroid. Motivated by tangles, a set $Z$ in a matroid $M$ has been defined to be $3$-connected if, for each $j$ in $\{1,2\}$, there is no $j$-separation $(X,Y)$ of $M$ such that each of $|Z \cap X|$ and $|Z \cap Y|$ is at least $j$. This paper solves a problem of Whittle for $k= 3$ by proving that a minor-minimal matroid having $Z$ as a $3$-connected set has at most $3|Z| - 4$ elements. We also identify the matroids for which this bound is attained.

title: On optimal (v,5,3,1) optical orthogonal codes
summary: In this paper, we establish a tight upper bound for the size of a $(v,5,3,1)$ optical orthogonal code (OOC) and call such a code optimal when it achieves this upper bound. In addition, if an optimal OOC has the property that all non-identity elements of $\mathbb{Z}_v$ are covered by the list of differences of its codeword-sets then it is called perfect. In this paper, we present direct and recursive constructions for infinite classes of optimal and perfect $(v,5,3,1)$-OOCs.

title: Facets of the X-ray polytope of doubly stochastic matrices
summary: We study the polytope of anti-diagonal X-rays of k x k doubly stochastic matrices, the image of the Birkhoff polytope under the map that sums the entries along each anti-diagonal. Its facets other than the coordinate facets are the minimal joint tail bounds for lattice laws of a sum of two dependent uniform random variables. We give an exact facet criterion in terms of the allowed edges of a tight graph. For rays of the underlying tropical fan, total support of the tight graph suffices for a facet but is not necessary, as an example with k=19 shows. Up to affine functions and positive scaling, the potentials that define a facet form a polytope whose vertices are its rays. Facets propagate by padding and by grid refinement under explicit hypotheses. We give infinite families of facets from no step potential, facets of quadratic height, superpolynomially many facets, and a classification of three-step potentials. Total support of a step potential is characterized by a Hall-type condition on block starts; with computer assistance, total support decides facets of step potentials for k<=26. The facet counts up to k=12 are found directly for k<=3 and, for k>=4, come from an enumeration by a provably complete algorithm; an independent exact recomputation reproduces its ray lists for 5<=k<=12.
comment: 36 pages, 4 tables; supplementary material (25 pages) as an ancillary file. Code and data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23440726 (https://github.com/methodtrace/2026-doubly-stochastic-xray-facets). Companion paper: arXiv:2610.24197

title: An Asymptotic for Non-Wieferich Numbers
summary: A cyclic number is a positive integer $n$ such that $\gcd(n, \varphi(n)) = 1$. Erdős showed that the number of cyclic numbers up to $x$, $C(x)$, has $C(x) \sim e^{-γ}x/\log_3(x)$ asymptotically as $x$ tends to infinity. We define Wieferich numbers to be odd, positive integers $n$ such that $(n, (2^{\ell(n)}-1)/n) > 1$, where $\ell(n)$ is the smallest positive integer with $2^{\ell(n)} \equiv 1 \mod n$. Franco and Pomerance showed that non-Wieferich numbers have density zero among the odd integers. We show that the counting function of $n \leq x$ in the symmetric difference of non-Wieferich numbers and cyclic numbers is $O(x/(\log_3(x))^2)$, under a mild assumption on the counting function of Wieferich primes.

title: A Counterexample to the Eventual Stability Conjecture
summary: We give a counterexample to the eventual stability conjecture over number fields and classify for power maps.

title: Schäffer's conjecture for even $k \le 42$
summary: In 1956, Schäffer made a conjecture on the whole number solutions to the Diophantine equation $S_k(x):=1^k+2^k+\cdots+x^k=y^n$. In this paper we show how for even $k$, we can descend to a long list of three coupled equations of the form $Ax^p-By^p=1$, where $A,B\in\mathbb{Q}$. To this system, we apply the modular method, linear forms in logarithms, and local methods. As a result, we prove Schäffer's conjecture for even $k \le 42$.

title: A quaternary Diophantine inequality with prime numbers of a special form (II)
summary: Let $N$ be a sufficiently large real number. In this paper, it is proved that, for $1<c<\frac{5179}{3909}$ and for any arbitrary large number $E>0$, the Diophantine inequality \begin{equation*} \big|p_1^c+p_2^c+p_3^c+p_4^c-N\big|<(\log N)^{-E} \end{equation*} is solvable in prime variables $p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4$ such that each of the numbers $p_i+2\,(i=1,2,3,4)$ has, counted according to multiplicity, at most $[\frac{31250}{5179-3909c}]$ prime factors, which constitutes a large improvement upon the previous results of Dimitrov [13] and Li-Xue-Zhang [22], respectively.

title: A relative Schinzel-Zassenhaus bound for the polynomial $T^2 - 1$
summary: For $f(T) = T^2 - 1$, we establish a lower bound for the relative dynamical house of wandering algebraic integers. This bound depends on the degree over the maximal abelian extension of the rationals. Our proof follows Dimitrov's approach to the Schinzel-Zassenhaus Conjecture and its generalization by Habegger-Schmidt.

title: Short sums of the Möbius function over function fields
summary: We develop a new method which allows us to estimate, with a power saving, sums of the M{ö}bius function over function fields $\F_p(X)$. The sums run over monic polynomials with all other coefficients in short intervals, of length below the Pólya--Vinogradov threshold $p^{1/2}$. A classical result of L.~Stickelberger (1898) reduces this question to bounding character sums with polynomial discriminants which are inhomogeneous multivariate polynomials. Variants of Burgess's method with non-linear shifts {\it {à} la carte} are introduced to go beyond the Pólya--Vinogradov range, combined with a stratification result of J. Xu (2020) for complete character sums.

title: Subset sums of power values over Galois rings
summary: Let $R=GR(p^m,p^{mf})$, where $p$ is prime, $q=p^f$, $m,f\geq1$, $d\geq2$ and $p\nmid d$. We count $n$-element subsets of $P=\{x^d:x\in R\}\setminus\{0\}$, the set of distinct nonzero $d$th-power values, with a prescribed sum. For fixed $m,d,n$ with $n\geq3$, the count equals \[ q^{-m}\binom{|P|}{n}(1+O_{m,d,n}(q^{1-n/2})) \] as $q\to\infty$ through admissible prime powers, uniformly over all targets and with both $p$ and $f$ allowed to vary. For fixed $m,d$, we also classify uniform relative equidistribution at the remaining positive sizes: it fails at $n=1$, and at $n=2$ it holds along an admissible sequence if and only if, for all sufficiently large terms, $\gcd(d,q-1)=1$ and $(m\geq2\text{ or }p\ne2)$.

title: On a conjecture of Velani
summary: We investigate the approximation of elements of the middle-third Cantor set by dyadic rationals, and natural extensions. We prove a conjecture of Velani, completing the metric theory for the Cantor measure. Our key method enables a quantitative study of the incommensurability of binary and ternary expansions of integers, initiated by Furstenberg. The method has other applications, e.g. $\sum_{k} |\hatμ(2^k)|^σ< \infty$ for any $σ> 0$, where $μ$ is the Cantor measure.

title: Hecke Orbits on Globally Drinfeld-Uniformized Shimura Varieties Are $p$-adically Nowhere Dense
summary: Fix a projective unitary Shimura datum satisfying Varshavsky's global Drinfeld uniformization hypotheses at a place $v\mid p$ of its reflex field $E$. Let $\mathcal{S}h$ be the base change of the Shimura variety to $\mathbb C_p$ at a sufficiently small neat finite level. We prove that for every closed reduced algebraic subvariety $Z\subset\mathcal{S}h$ with $\operatorname{dim} Z<\operatorname{dim} \mathcal{S}h$, the $p$-adic closure of its full finite adelic Hecke orbit has empty interior in $\mathcal{S}h(\mathbb C_p)$. At certain compatible levels, the nowhere density theorem also holds for Shimura varieties associated with a related PEL datum having the same adjoint datum as Varshavsky's. Moreover, for every rational prime $p$ and every integer $d\geq2$, there is a projective unitary Shimura variety of dimension $d-1$ satisfying these uniformization hypotheses at a place above $p$ for which the nowhere density theorem holds.

title: The Octonionic Rational Wave Numbers: Non-Associative Sequence Algebras, Moufang Loops, and Exceptional $G_2$ Symmetries
summary: We generalize discrete rational wave numbers (arXiv:2609.23233) to the octonionic rational wave numbers $\mathbb{O}^\mathbb{Z}$ over Cayley's octonions $\mathbb{O}$. Rather than assuming higher imaginary units, all rational wave number spaces $\mathbb{C}^\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{H}^\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{O}^\mathbb{Z}$ are derived constructively from two scalar primitives: the coordinate advance $E_Z$ and phase calibration $E_{\bar{1}}$. Their closure under pointwise multiplication, inversion, and rational roots generates an infinite divisible Moufang loop on the sequence ring $\mathcal{S}_\mathbb{O} := \mathbb{O}^\mathbb{Z}$, terminating strictly at $\mathbb{O}^\mathbb{Z}$ via sedenionic zero-divisor excision. By Artin's Theorem, pairwise compositions remain strictly associative, whereas three-wave interactions generate an intrinsic non-associative curvature quantified by the associator $[u, v, w] = (uv)w - u(vw)$. We define a real-valued sequence inner product that bypasses the Jordan--von Neumann--Wigner obstruction, establishing the orthonormality of the seven Fano coordinate primitives. We establish three principal theorems: (1) The Invariant Hexagonal Mesh Theorem, proving that cumulative integration exhibits a scale-invariant bifurcation at $n=6$ governed by the root system of $G_2 = \operatorname{Aut}(\mathbb{O})$ and its $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ stabilizer subgroup; (2) The Algebraic Phase Jitter Theorem, showing that Catalan parenthesization trees across non-Fano triads produce an irreducible zero-point phase fluctuation, yielding an algebraic origin for vacuum jitter; and (3) The Rational Loop Closure Theorem, proving that rational frequencies select closed finite Moufang sub-loops, while irrational frequencies yield topologically dense, non-closing trajectories. This provides an autonomous, discrete algebraic foundation for non-associative geometry and fundamental physical symmetries.

title: Zeros of quadratic Dirichlet $L$-functions
summary: We consider Dirichlet $L$-functions $L(s, χ)$ where $χ$ is a quadratic character to modulus $q$. We show that for $χ$ even (resp. odd) $L(σ, χ)\neq 0$ for all $σ>0$ provided that $q\leq 10^{9}$ (resp. $q\leq 10^{10})$. In particular, this result rules out Siegel--Landau zeros for such $L$-functions. Combined, these results improve on previous work by nearly four orders of magnitude. We also list some applications of this work.

title: Construction of Galois modules describing ideal class groups and applications to Iwasawa theory
summary: For a finite Galois extension of number fields, the ideal class groups of intermediate fields do not behave well under taking Galois coinvariants in general. In this paper, we construct a Galois module whose Galois coinvariants explicitly describe the ideal class groups of the intermediate fields. As an application, we demonstrate how this construction naturally yields some results in classical Iwasawa theory.

title: Mixed sums of infinite multiple zeta-star values with restricted indices
summary: We study arithmetic sums of infinite multiple zeta-star values subject to upper or lower bounds on their indices. Let $η(\mathcal D_q)$ be the image, under the zeta-star correspondence, of the admissible infinite index sequences with all indices at most $q$, and let $\overline{η(\mathcal T_p)}$ be the closure of the image of the sequences with all indices at least $p$. We prove that $η(\mathcal D_q)+\overline{η(\mathcal T_p)}$ is an interval exactly when $p\leq q$; in that case it is $[ζ^\star(\{q\}^{\infty})+1,\infty)$. We also show that sums of two upper-bounded sets are half-lines, even with different bounds, whereas sums of two lower-bounded sets are never intervals. The proofs combine a uniform product estimate with natural gap constructions. Lateral thickness handles the diagonal case $p=q\geq3$, while a non-strict local bridge--gap criterion treats $p=q=2$ directly. Compact truncations and explicit omitted intervals yield the remaining assertions.

title: Statistics of entries of matrices from the general linear group over a finite field
summary: Let $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$ be the group of $n\times n$ invertible matrices over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$. How many matrices in $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$ are there with a subset of their entries prescribed? Motivated by the random matrix theory of classical compact groups, we address this question and various variants, with a focus on asymptotic results that are valid as $n$ tends to infinity. Our methods are Fourier-analytic, with the main input being an exponential sum over $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$, evaluated in 1955 by Hodges via elementary methods. Our results turn out to be related to investigations carried out in other fields, including coding theory, universality for $p$-adic matrices and algebraic combinatorics.

title: Ideal class groups of certain real quadratic number fields and factorizations of values of certain quadratic polynomials
summary: We determine the odd primes $p$ for which the number of distinct prime divisors of $d-x^2$ is at most $2$ for every positive odd integers $x\leq\sqrt{p}$. We also determine the odd primes $p$ for which the number of distinct prime divisors of $2p-x^2$ is at most $2$ for every positive even integers $x\leq\sqrt{2p}$. To this end, we show that these properties of $p$ and $2p$ impose restrictions on the class numbers and fundamental units of the real quadratic fields ${\mathbb Q}(\sqrt{p})$ and ${\mathbb Q}(\sqrt{2p})$.

title: Computing Theta Characteristics and their Galois action on general curves of moderate genus
summary: In this article, we present an algorithm that, given a smooth curve $X$ defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, returns an explicit arithmetic representation of both odd and even Theta Characteristics split by parity. It allows us to retrieve their Galois action and étale algebra. The output includes the Theta Hyperplanes of the Theta Characteristics when they are finite, their associated proof functions as well as the dictionary of their quadratic forms. The algorithm works in a rather large generality as it handles any one-equation (potentially singular) model of smooth curves. The most binding requirement remains the necessity for an explicit degree 1 rational divisor on the curve or more likely a rational point. We implemented the algorithm and give examples up to genus $5$.

title: The exceptional set of Goldbach numbers within the set of squares
summary: We prove that the set of numbers of type $n = 2m^2$ below $X$ which cannot be written as a sum of two primes has cardinality at most $X^{19/24 + o(1)}$.

title: Residue Sums Modulo Products of Two Distinct Odd Primes
summary: Let $S_m(a)$ denote the sum of the least positive residues in one multiplicative period of $a$ modulo $m$, of length $k$. We study the equality $S_m(a)=mk/2$ for $m=pq$, where $p,q$ are distinct odd primes and $k$ is even. Complementary pairing settles subgroups containing $-1$; the remaining cases depend on their embedding in the two local unit groups. At index four, we exclude mixed cyclic subgroups with biquadratic annihilator and classify every eligible imprimitive quartic kernel using two odd integer moments at its prime conductor. For each fixed conductor, the proportion of admissible second primes giving equality is $1/4$ or $1/2$; full coset balance has proportion $1/4$. For primitive quartic characters, classical triangular character-sum identities yield explicit short-sum criteria, and the relative class-number formula gives an obstruction to a centered coset. At index six, we give structural counts and construct an infinite family modulo $19q$ in which nonzero sextic and quadratic moments cancel. These applications use a standard odd-character expansion, which also recovers the known index-two balance classification and determines the sign of its deviation. A reproducible census for $pq\le10000$ counts $75\,090$ eligible cyclic subgroups and identifies $101$ mixed index-four subgroups whose own sum is centered although some coset sums are not.

title: Perturbing the Conway sequence
summary: We study the alternating perturbation of Conway's nested recurrence, $C(n)=C(C(n-1))+C(n-C(n-1))+(-1)^n$ for $n\geq 3$, with $C(1)=C(2)=1$. We prove that the sequence is well defined and satisfies $C(n)=ψ^{-3}n+O(n/\sqrt{\log n})$, where $ψ>1$ is the real root of $ψ^3=ψ^2+1$.

title: On the Gauss sphere problem
summary: In this article we improve Heath-Brown's estimate for the error term in the three-dimensional sphere problem, proving \[ \#\{\mathbf x\in\mathbb Z^3:\|\mathbf x\|\le R\}=\frac{4π}{3}R^3+O_\varepsilon(R^{55/42+\varepsilon}). \] Incoporating the recent OpenAI quasi-GRH into our argument further improves this to \[ \#\{\mathbf x\in\mathbb Z^3:\|\mathbf x\|\le R\}= \frac{4π}{3}R^3+O_\varepsilon(R^{\frac{2274811}{1743872}+\varepsilon}). \]

title: Sharp spherical $L^p\to L^4$ extension estimates over finite fields in odd dimensions
summary: Let $q$ be an odd prime power, let $d\ge3$ be odd, and let $S_j=\{ξ\in \mathbb F_q^d:ξ_1^2+\cdots+ξ_d^2=j\}$, where $j\ne 0$. We prove the sharp extension estimate ${L^{4(d+1)/(3d+1)}(S_j, dσ)\to L^4(\mathbb F_q^d,dc)}$ whenever $η_q((-1)^{(d-1)/2}j)=-1$, where $η_q$ is the quadratic character. This confirms the odd-dimensional spherical extension conjecture of Koh, Pham, and Vinh over every finite field of odd characteristic. Together with the known estimate in the complementary sign class, this determines the sharp ${L^p\to{L^4}}$ extension range for all nonzero-radius spheres in odd dimensions. We also apply the endpoint estimate to obtain sufficient conditions for the unique recovery of sparse signals from incomplete Fourier data.

title: Integer symplectic matrices in expanding boxes
summary: We prove an essentially optimal uniform upper bound for the number of integer symplectic matrices inside a box of expanding side length and arbitrary centre.

title: Integral trace forms of cyclic number fields without tameness
summary: Let $K/\mathbf{Q}$ be a cyclic number field and let $T_K=\bigl(\mathcal{O}_K,(x,y)\mapsto \operatorname{Tr}_{K/\mathbf{Q}}(xy)\bigr)$ be its integral trace lattice. We prove that two cyclic number fields have isometric integral trace lattices if and only if they have the same degree, signature, and signed discriminant. More generally, an isomorphism between the Dirichlet character groups of two finite abelian extensions that preserves the conductor and parity of every character yields an isometry of their integral trace lattices, equivariant for the dual identification of Galois groups. For cyclic fields, the degree, signature, and discriminant determine the character group together with these two functions. This proves Bolaños's conjecture for wildly ramified cyclic fields and gives the corresponding extension of the tame classification: in general, the signature must be retained as an additional invariant.

title: On the notion of reasonable functions in Cohen--Lenstra type heuristics
summary: We elucidate the notion of "reasonable functions" in the context of Cohen--Lenstra heuristics. For a sequence $(x_i)_i$ of independent random variables valued in an infinite discrete probability space $(X,p)$, we investigate for what sets $S$ of functions on $X$ it is true that almost surely, for all $f\in S$, the average of $f$ on the sequence is equal to its expected value. We show that if $p$ decays sufficiently quickly, as e.g. the Cohen--Lenstra distribution does, then $\bigcup_{q>1}L^q(X)$ is such a set; while if $p$ decays sufficiently slowly, then not even $\bigcap_{q<\infty}L^q(X)$ has this property.

title: Squarefree values of random polynomials are Gaussian mixtures
summary: Fix $d\ge1$ and choose a polynomial $P$ uniformly at random from the set of integer polynomials of degree $d$ whose coefficients have absolute value at most $H$. We study $E_{P}$, the error in the count of squarefree values $P(n)$ for $n\leq x$. In the range $x=H^{o\left(1\right)}$, we prove that $E_{P}\left(x\right)/x^{\frac{1}{4}}$ converges to a Gaussian mixture that is not itself Gaussian, $\sqrt{C\left(G\right)}Z$, where $G$ is the weak limit, as $H\rightarrow\infty$, of the prime-indexed vector $\left(P\bmod p^{2}\right)_{p}$, $C$ is a nonnegative function and $Z$ is an independent standard Gaussian. This answers a question of Sofos. Finally, in the appendix, we establish that $\log \mathbb{E}[C(G)^m]\asymp_d m^2/(\log m)^2$ as $m\to\infty$.

title: A Sharp Bound for Additive Complements
summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be infinite sets of nonnegative integers whose sum contains all sufficiently large integers, and let $A(x)$ and $B(x)$ be their counting functions. We give a discrete proof of the sharp implication \[ \limsup_{x\to\infty}\frac{A(x)B(x)}{x}<\frac32 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad A(x)B(x)-x\longrightarrow+\infty. \] The constant $3/2$ is best possible. Using finite convolution sums, we show that a long gap in one set forces a gap in the other. We then compare the counting functions before and after the gap to obtain the sharp bound.

title: Zeros of $E_2$, quasi-periods, and Schwarz maps
summary: We study the zeros of the Eisenstein series $E_2$, their distribution near rational cusps, and the values of modular functions at these zeros. Using Watson's inversion formula, we prove that the number of zeros in $0\leq\operatorname{Re}τ<1$ with imaginary part at least $Y$ satisfies \[ N(Y)=\frac{1}{2πY} +O\!\left(Y^{-1/2}\log\frac1Y\right) \qquad(Y\to0^+). \] We also determine the limiting distribution of the scaled displacements from the cusps and prove that two zeros whose difference is rational differ by an integer. At every zero $ρ$, classical transcendence theorems imply that both $j(ρ)$ and $λ(ρ)$ are transcendental. We use this fact to obtain an exact multiplicity formula for arithmetic quasimodular forms at arbitrary congruence level and to show that all ordinary derivatives of arithmetic modular functions on congruence subgroups, evaluated at $ρ$, are algebraic over $\overline{\mathbb Q}(j(ρ),j'(ρ))$. We then relate Watson's formula to the Schwarz map of a rational transform of the Legendre hypergeometric equation. Finally, we give conditional results on the transcendence of $ρ$ under modular Schanuel and period conjectures, and determine why the associated analytic subgroup fails the rank condition in Waldschmidt's theorem.

title: Kelly's conjectures on Condorcet winner probabilities for odd electorates
summary: Let $C(m,n)$ denote the probability that, among $n$ independent uniformly random permutations of $m$ labels, there exists a label that precedes every other label in a strict majority of the permutations. We prove that $C(m,n)>C(m,n+2)$ for $m \ge 3$ and odd $n \ge 1$, and that $C(m,n)>C(m+1,n)$ for $m \ge 2$ and odd $n \ge 3$. These results establish Kelly's two monotonicity conjectures for odd electorates. The proofs use integral representations involving probabilities associated with sums of independent Bernoulli random variables.

title: Painlevé representations for joint moments of characteristic polynomials from the orthogonal and unitary symplectic groups
summary: We study joint moments of characteristic polynomials and their second derivatives for Haar-distributed matrices from the unitary symplectic and orthogonal groups. We establish their large-$N$ asymptotics throughout the full admissible range of the moment parameters and identify the limiting coefficients probabilistically in terms of the first inverse power sum of the Bessel point process. This extends the corresponding results of Assiotis, Gunes, Keating, and Wei [Proc. Lond. Math. Soc., 132 (2026), e70136] to the full admissible parameter range. Throughout this full range, we also express these limits in terms of a distinguished solution of the $σ$-Painlevé III' equation. Our approach reduces the problem to singular inverse-power statistics of the Jacobi unitary ensemble and combines their finite-$N$ $σ$-Painlevé V representation with a refined Riemann-Hilbert analysis yielding precise small-$x$ asymptotics and uniform derivative estimates for the finite-$N$ correction term. A key ingredient in the probabilistic identification is a kernel-based proof that the rescaled first inverse power sum of the Jacobi ensemble converges in distribution to its Bessel point process counterpart.

title: Outer automorphisms of HNN extensions of abelian groups
summary: Let $G$ be a commensurating HNN extension of a finitely generated free abelian group. We characterise when $\mathrm{Out}(G)$ is finitely generated and derive structural information about the group. We give soluble and non-soluble examples of commensurating HNN extensions of finitely generated free abelian groups with outer automorphism group not finitely generated.

title: On Finite Groups with Element Order Set of Width 3
summary: We study finite groups in which every element order is divisible by at most three distinct primes. We determine the possible nonabelian composition factors, prove that a nonabelian simple group with this property has at most $15$ prime divisors in its order, and deduce that $ρ(G)\leq192$ for every finite group $G$ with $α(G)\leq3$.

title: The first $\ell^2$-Betti number, cost and rank gradient of few-relator random groups
summary: Let $G$ be a random group in the few-relator model with $n\ge 2$ generators and $m\ge 1$ relators. We prove that asymptotically almost surely the first $\ell^2$-Betti number, the cost minus one, and the absolute rank gradient of $G$ are all equal to $\max\{n-m-1,0\}$. In particular, the equality $β_1^{(2)}(G)=0$ when $m\ge n-1$ answers positively a conjecture of Kielak, Kropholler and Wilkes [J. Lond. Math. Soc., 2022].

title: Kobayashi's problem for power semigroups of inverse semigroups
summary: For a semigroup $S$ (written multiplicatively), let $\mathcal P(S)$ denote the semigroup of all non-empty subsets of $S$ under setwise multiplication. The finitary power semigroup $\mathcal P_\text{fin}(S)$ is the subsemigroup of $\mathcal P(S)$ consisting of all non-empty finite subsets of $S$. Kobayashi's problem asks for which classes $\mathcal O$ of semigroups every isomorphism $\mathcal P(H) \to \mathcal P(K)$ with $H, K \in \mathcal O$ maps singletons bijectively onto singletons and hence induces an isomorphism $H \to K$. We give an affirmative answer for inverse semigroups, extending previous results for groups, semilattices, and, more generally, Clifford semigroups. We also establish the corresponding rigidity theorem for finitary power semigroups. To this end, we develop a new framework that provides a common approach to both settings.

title: The Conjugacy Problem for Recursively Presented Virtually Soluble Groups of Finite Prüfer Rank
summary: We solve a long-standing conjugacy problem for finitely presented soluble groups of finite Prüfer rank, recorded as Problem~9.52 in the Kourovka Notebook, in the stronger setting of recursively presented finitely generated virtually soluble groups. Robinson proved that, in every recursively presented finitely generated virtually soluble minimax group, conjugacy to any fixed element is decidable, while explicitly lefting open whether the procedure could be made uniform in the target element. We establish this uniformity. More specifically, we prove that every recursively presented finitely generated virtually soluble group of finite Prüfer rank has decidable Conjugacy Problem.

title: On unit groups of purely infinite rings
summary: We prove that the unit group of any purely infinite, regular, right self-injective ring admits a universal sequence of words (thus has strong distortion), is minimally almost periodic, has finite involution width, is verbally simple and verbally elliptic, and has uncountable uniform strong cofinality. These findings are consequences of more refined structural results, some of which provide concrete cardinal estimates involving the Goodearl--Boyle dimension of the ring. A central ingredient in our results is a comprehensive study of bounded normal generation, in particular with respect to certain classes of involutions. Along the way, we develop some abstract methods and concepts pertaining to geometric group theory.

title: The Diophantine Problem with constraints in some free-by-cyclic groups
summary: In this paper we explore the Diophantine Problem, that is, the solvability of equations, in one-relator and free-by-cyclic groups, showing that this is decidable in some cases and undecidable otherwise, depending on their abelianisation and centre. In particular, we focus on a version of the Diophantine Problem which asks about the existence of solutions satisfying abelianisation constraints, and prove a number of results concerning the decidability of this problem for free-by-cyclic groups with centre, tree-GBS groups, cyclically pinched groups and the first hydra group.
